title: Regional Failover: The Replica Is Ninety Seconds Behind
businessContext: A regional failure isolates the primary order database. The standby is asynchronous and 90 seconds behind. The business recovery-point objective is 30 seconds, and the old primary may still be accepting writes from internal workers.
problemStatement: Public order writes fail in region A; the region B standby is reachable but has not replayed the latest acknowledged orders. Work through three timed developments, justify your actions, and write an evidence-based incident response. The simulation starts paused; advancing time can expire unanswered decisions.
constraints: Do not promise zero data loss with asynchronous replication.
Escalate any recovery-point breach and preserve reconciliation evidence.
All telemetry is synthetic. Actions only affect this practice simulation.
candidateTasks: Contain customer impact while preserving evidence and data integrity.
Respond to each new development and explain the selected action.
Cite telemetry supporting the root cause; distinguish observation from inference.
Define a permanent correction, regression coverage, recovery gates, and stakeholder update.

hints: The initial replay gap is 90 seconds versus a 30-second RPO.
Fence every old writer path using the reviewed infrastructure mechanism and confirm enforcement.
Automate failover authority, fencing checks and writer routing as one tested runbook.
alternativeApproaches: Wait for primary recovery if the expected delay is preferable to the measured data-loss risk.
Use synchronous replication for workloads whose durability requirement justifies its latency and availability trade-offs.
commonMistakes: Equating a reachable standby with a current standby.
Using DNS as the only fencing mechanism.
Automatically failing back to the old primary without divergence analysis.
